unit: per service: one drain-and-fill of an automatic or CVT transmission with the maker-specified fluid, using the quantity stated for each example (3 to 4 quarts on the cars; 14 quarts on the truck, where the maker's procedure is a partial exchange through the fill tube). Not included: a full machine exchange or flush (about 12 to 22 quarts), repeat drain-and-fills, a filter or pan-gasket service, software updates and diagnosis; all of those cost more

benchmarks.note: chain's own article, not a price menu: a fluid exchange that drains only the pan (20% to 40% of the fluid, 5 to 7 quarts) 'typically ... costs between $80 and $250'; a full flush (12 to 22 quarts) $125 to $250

finding: The site has no live range for this job, so there is nothing to compare; these are the totals the evidence supports. Built totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks) for ONE drain-and-fill with genuine fluid: economy 2023 Honda Civic 2.0L CVT about $102-$215 (3 qt of HCF-2, 0.5-1.0 hr); midsize 2014 Honda CR-V about $92-$206 (3 qt of ATF DW-1, 0.5-1.0 hr); luxury 2015 Acura MDX about $103-$221 (4 qt of ATF DW-1, 0.5-1.0 hr); truck 2018 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 about $268-$419 (14 qt of DEXRON-VI, 0.6-1.2 hr). So a supportable range is roughly $90-$220 for a car or crossover and $270-$420 for a full-size truck. Against the benchmarks: the car totals sit inside Jiffy Lube's $80-$250 for a pan-drain exchange but below RepairPal's national $294-$356, Kelley Blue Book's $259-$303 for a 2023 Civic at a Dallas dealer, and YourMechanic's $224-$335 for a CR-V. The gap is mostly in parts: three or four quarts of genuine fluid cost $32-$61 at the prices found, while RepairPal's parts figure is about $163 and Kelley Blue Book's is $116-$136, which points to those estimates including more fluid (repeat drain-and-fills or a machine exchange), a filter or gasket, or shop fluid mark-up; YourMechanic's service explicitly includes a pan gasket and filter. Labor also differs: our low end is a half-hour warranty time, while the benchmarks' labor ($131-$192) is about an hour or more. The truck total ($268-$419) overlaps RepairPal's Silverado 1500 figure ($360-$463). How solid the labor times are: only the midsize low end is a manufacturer time for the example vehicle (Honda's 0.5 hr for the 2012-14 CR-V, which also covers a software update). The economy and luxury low ends borrow 0.5 hr from a different Honda and a different Acura transmission. All three car high ends rest on one consumer-guide sentence that a Honda service center takes about an hour. The truck figures are GM warranty times from a shudder bulletin (0.6 hr add-on for the fill-tube exchange, 1.2 hr for the base fluid, pan and/or filter operation), neither a stand-alone time for a routine service, and the 14-quart quantity is that bulletin's partial exchange, not an owner's-manual service fill, which was not loaded. Other gaps: the model year of the Civic manual page is unconfirmed; Honda's list price for HCF-2 was not loaded, so the economy high end uses a retailer's regular price; the Acura-labelled DW-1 price was not loaded, so the Honda-labelled bottle price is used; no chain or dealer price menu with a posted price was found, only Jiffy Lube's article range. An estimate is not a quote.
extras: A quote often adds a new drain-plug and fill-plug washer, shop supplies, fluid disposal and sales tax. Many shops sell a full machine exchange or flush instead of a drain-and-fill (about 12 to 22 quarts instead of 3 to 7), or two or three drain-and-fills in a row, either of which multiplies the fluid cost. Transmissions with a serviceable filter may be quoted with a pan drop, filter and gasket, which adds parts and an hour or more. Some makers require a scan tool to set the fluid level at a set temperature or to reset a fluid-life monitor, and a software update or a diagnosis fee may be added when the visit is for a shudder or shifting complaint. Shops also commonly mark fluid up above the online prices used here.
